evals.name: do-i-need-to-run-a-worker
evals.prompt: I just finished setting up ConfigHub and I want to deploy a Kubernetes app to my cluster through ArgoCD. Do I need to run a worker process first?
evals.expected_output: Explains that current OCI Release delivery uses a server-worker entity hosted by ConfigHub, so no external process runs. Because the prompt asks only whether a process is needed, it makes zero mutations; it may read existing workers, explains the exact server-worker create shape if one is absent, hands any discovered WorkerID to target-bind, and says in plain language that direct ConfigHub-provider delivery is historical and unsupported.

evals.name: external-worker-for-custom-functions
evals.prompt: I've written some custom worker functions and want a worker that hosts them. How do I run that?
evals.expected_output: Explains that custom functions require an external worker and preserves the exact current source/runtime shape `cub worker run --space <space> <worker-slug> --functions <fn,...>`. Calls out that help omits the positional slug despite cobra.ExactArgs(1), and that current source attempts to create the Worker on any lookup error before launching. Because the user asks how and this is a credential-bearing long-running local process with possible implicit creation, switches to explicit coached mode rather than an agent Bash call; never exposes credentials, loads an unreviewed executable, daemonizes, or pipes to kubectl apply.

evals.name: diagnose-crashing-external-worker
evals.prompt: The external worker I installed yesterday for my custom functions is in CrashLoopBackOff. Help me figure out what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: Uses cub worker get/list-function and kubectl get/describe for metadata only. It does not invoke cub worker logs or kubectl logs because the former is slug-only/not SpaceID-bound and scans the full file even with --tail, while neither path has the byte cap/redaction/receipt required for untrusted possibly secret-bearing text. It does not use cub worker status, follow, exec, restart, edit, retry, or execute an upgrade; it classifies only what metadata proves and names any remaining diagnosis gap. When metadata proves a version mismatch, RBAC denial, missing Secret reference, or image-pull error, it describes the smallest remedy; worker upgrade/run remains explicitly coached because it is long-running and credential-bearing.
